R01.rationale: The delivery promise constrains fulfillment quality; it does not specify an independent software capability.

R07.rationale: Phone-only ordering is explicitly replaced by web ordering in R32 and extended by SMS in R37.

R08.rationale: The phone interaction is retired by R32; customer identification remains in R09/R11, and R37 reuses the company number for SMS.

R20.rationale: Attaching a label to a bag is physical work, supported by software label generation in R19.

R26.rationale: R35 replaces handwritten confirmation. Keeping the customer's invoice copy remains physical process context under R21.

R33.rationale: The browser/version compatibility list is an unspecified platform constraint, retained as assumption A01.

R34.rationale: Defines future user groups and removes phone clerks; does not establish new administration use cases.

clauses.text: Offer prepackaged breakfasts containing a defined selection of products, such as mini-breakfast and luxury breakfast.
clauses.review_note: Examples describe offered packages; no new product administration functionality is inferred.

clauses.text: Customers can assemble an individual breakfast by choosing simple products.
clauses.review_note: Preserves customer composition of a breakfast.

clauses.text: A prepackaged product can contain simple products and other prepackaged products.
clauses.review_note: Preserves recursive product composition; cycle handling is unspecified.

clauses.text: An order consists of quantities of simple products and prepackaged products.
clauses.review_note: Retains order-line quantities and both product types.

clauses.text: Each product has a unit of measure and a price per unit in euros.
clauses.review_note: Preserves unit-based pricing.

clauses.text: A customer number consists of a two-digit area code, seven customer digits, and a one-digit checksum.
clauses.review_note: Format retained; the checksum computation is not specified.

clauses.text: Each order belongs to one customer; collective orders for several customers are not allowed.
clauses.review_note: Preserves the single-customer invariant.

clauses.text: Authenticate the customer before allowing her to assemble an order.
clauses.review_note: R32/R34 replace the clerk interaction with application behavior.

clauses.text: Check that a customer is not blacklisted before allowing her to order.
clauses.review_note: Eligibility is a separate obligation from verifying identity.

clauses.text: An authenticated eligible customer can add one or more named products to the shopping cart.
clauses.review_note: Direct product selection remains after phone-clerk retirement.

clauses.text: Search for suitable products by requested characteristics, including a calorie limit and a price limit.
clauses.review_note: R36 replaces the clerk-mediated search; the criteria remain applicable.

clauses.text: A customer can use one of her previous orders as a blueprint for a new order.
clauses.review_note: Preserves ownership of the previous order and follow-up ordering.

clauses.text: Within one order, customers can combine direct product selection, product search results, and a previous-order blueprint.
clauses.review_note: Expands 'those three methods' using R11-R13; removes retired clerk wording under R32.

clauses.text: An order can reference at most one blueprint order.
clauses.review_note: Preserves the at-most-one constraint, including the possibility of no blueprint.

clauses.text: An order can serve as the blueprint for many subsequent orders.
clauses.review_note: Preserves blueprint reuse without imposing a usage limit.

clauses.text: Each customer has exactly one predefined delivery address, which is reused when placing an order.
clauses.review_note: Separates the address rule from order-number assignment in the same statement.

clauses.text: Assign an order number consisting of eight digits with a checksum and communicate it to the customer after ordering.
clauses.review_note: Eight base digits plus checksum is a working interpretation consistent with R41's example; checksum algorithm remains open.

clauses.text: Display each order and its ordered products to the packing clerk for assembly.
clauses.review_note: Software support inferred from automation in R32; physical bag packing remains process context.

clauses.text: The packing clerk assigns a delivery clerk to an order.
clauses.review_note: Extracts the assignment operation embedded in the label description.

clauses.text: Print a bag label with the packing clerk name, customer first name and surname, delivery address, order number, and assigned delivery clerk.
clauses.review_note: R32 replaces the text processor; all listed label fields are preserved.

clauses.text: The packing clerk prints two copies of an order invoice.
clauses.review_note: R32 replaces the old text processor without changing the number of copies.

clauses.text: An invoice contains the packing clerk, customer name and address, order number, delivery clerk, ordered products, quantities, prices, and sum total.
clauses.review_note: Expands 'same data as the label' from R19; retains invoice-specific financial fields.

clauses.text: Every printed invoice copy receives a separate copy number, including copies printed again later.
clauses.review_note: Preserves separate numbering for each print, not just a version per order.

clauses.text: Calculate an optimal delivery itinerary that can fulfill multiple orders on one trip.
clauses.review_note: R32 replaces spreadsheet calculation. The optimization objective is unspecified.

clauses.text: The delivery clerk can print the calculated itinerary for the corresponding orders.
clauses.review_note: Extracts software printing; taking bags and driving remain physical process context.

clauses.text: A customer can look up an order by its order number and learn whether its delivery clerk is already on the way.
clauses.review_note: R32 removes phone interaction while preserving status information.

clauses.text: A customer can request cancellation of an order by giving its order number.
clauses.review_note: R32 removes the phone clerk; R29-R31 still constrain cancellation.

clauses.text: Once an order has been assembled, cancellation is no longer allowed.
clauses.review_note: Preserves the exact assembly cutoff; does not change it to dispatch.

clauses.text: An order cancellation cannot be undone.
clauses.review_note: Preserves irreversible cancellation.

clauses.text: Updating an existing order is not allowed.
clauses.review_note: Separates prohibition of update from the supported replacement workflow.

clauses.text: To change an order, a customer must cancel it and place a new order.
clauses.review_note: The replacement workflow remains subject to the cancellation cutoff.

clauses.text: Customers place orders through a web application, replacing ordering by phone.
clauses.review_note: Represents the web entry point; R19/R24/R25 preserve the individual replacement capabilities.

clauses.text: Confirm delivery when the customer enters her password in a browser on the delivery clerk's smartphone.
clauses.review_note: Supersedes handwritten confirmation in R26; preserves customer authentication at handover.

clauses.text: Allow browser-based product search without requiring authentication.
clauses.review_note: Retains public search access, distinct from authenticated ordering.

clauses.text: Accept SMS orders at the company number using the defined C customer-number W password P product-code quantity format.
clauses.review_note: Retains the SMS input contract and credentials. It invokes existing ordering rules rather than creating separate SMS business rules.

clauses.text: Every product has a unique product code.
clauses.review_note: The identifier is a product property even though SMS motivates its use.

clauses.text: An SMS order can contain any number of product entries within the general SMS message-length limit.
clauses.review_note: No new arbitrary product-count limit or fixed SMS character limit is introduced.

clauses.text: Respond to an SMS order with a text message containing the assigned order number.
clauses.review_note: Transport-specific response; the number is assigned by the shared ordering behavior.

clauses.text: Accept an SMS cancellation request in the format O followed by the order number.
clauses.review_note: Cancellation eligibility remains governed by R29-R31; sender authentication is unspecified.

clauses.text: Provide the existing payment system with expected-payment records containing customer number, order number, amount in euros, and expected payment date.
clauses.review_note: The payment system remains external; the expected-date policy is not invented.

clauses.text: When the packing clerk finishes assembling an order, transfer its expected-payment record to the existing payment system.
clauses.review_note: Preserves assembly completion as trigger, rather than invoice printing or dispatch.

clauses.text: Automatically print a business report for the manager every night covering orders of a given day.
clauses.review_note: Preserves scheduling and physical report output; business-day cutoff is unspecified.

clauses.text: The daily business report lists products, quantities, packing clerk, delivery clerk, customer, customer address, and order number for the day's orders.
clauses.review_note: Separates reporting content from nightly scheduling without removing any listed fields.
